text: In Watson-Crick base pairing within B-form DNA, how many hydrogen bonds form between guanine and cytosine compared to adenine and thymine?
choices: G-C forms 2 hydrogen bonds; A-T forms 3
Both base pairs form exactly 3 hydrogen bonds
G-C forms 4 hydrogen bonds; A-T forms 2
G-C forms 3 hydrogen bonds; A-T forms 2
explanation: Guanine and cytosine pair through 3 hydrogen bonds, while adenine and thymine pair through 2, which is why GC-rich DNA regions have higher melting temperatures. Swapping the counts, claiming both pairs have 3 bonds, or inflating the G-C count to 4 all misstate the well-established base-pairing chemistry.
